turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Rao, please sit. I checked the pressure outside, it is one thirty eight over eighty six, and the pulse is ninety two.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah, one second, this screen has frozen again. Sorry. Yes, what brings you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Toe.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Toe? Which one, can you repeat, I was not looking.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Right big.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, from last night it is paining very badly. He could not wear his chappal this morning.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right big toe, painful since last night. Is there fever?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): And swelling, is swelling there?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Swollen and red, shiny type. He was awake the whole night, tossing only.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): On a scale of one to ten, how much is the pain?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Beer.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Beer? I asked how bad the pain is. Please say it again, mild or severe.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Severe.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Severe, okay. Did you hit it anywhere, any injury?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): No injury. Has this happened before?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Year back.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the system beeped. Say that again?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Same. Year back.
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Same kind of pain, about a year back. Left side that time, I think. It settled in a few days with rest.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Similar episode about a year ago. Is any other joint paining now?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): What tablets do you take?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Water tablet.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Water tablet. I need the name, can you repeat the name?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Don't know.
[SEG0029] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hydrochlorothiazide, twelve point five milligram, one in the morning, for his BP. Two years he is taking it.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): HCTZ twelve point five milligrams each morning, for blood pressure. Did he take anything for this pain at home?
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One Crocin last night, five hundred milligram. No use at all.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Crocin is paracetamol, five hundred, one dose, no relief. Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Brufen gives him burning in the stomach. Is that an allergy?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Not allergy.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not an allergy then, only burning when he takes ibuprofen. I will remember that. Do you drink?
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Weekends.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): You said beer a minute ago. Beer, yes?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much beer?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): Few.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Few what? Say it properly, I missed it.
[SEG0043] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two or three bottles, Saturday and Sunday only. Weekdays he does not touch it.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Smoking?
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): Shall I take the sock off, doctor? It feels quite warm from here itself.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, kindly. One moment, I am opening the old file.
[SEG0048] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We were stuck at the signal twenty minutes, that is why we came late, sorry.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): No problem. Right first toe joint is swollen, red, warm, and he pulls away when I press. No wound. Foot pulses are good.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): Chair.
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chair? What chair, please repeat, I was typing.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Kicked. Yesterday.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): You kicked something yesterday? Just now you said no injury.
[SEG0054] person_3 (PATIENT): Small.
[SEG0055] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The dining chair, yesterday evening. He knocked the toe and said it was nothing only.

[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): A small knock yesterday evening, then this by night. I am thinking of gout, the joint is very typical, and there is the water tablet, the weekend beer, and that episode a year back. I will not stamp it as gout yet. The knock itself can flare a joint, and an infection in the joint I cannot rule out just by looking.
[SEG0057] person_3 (PATIENT): Gout?
[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): It is possible, not confirmed. I will not decide till the blood comes. I am sending serum uric acid, a blood count, and creatinine, because of the water tablet.
[SEG0059] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My brother was given colchicine once. Will you give that, or some pain tablet?

[SEG0060] person_2 (DOCTOR): For this, colchicine or an anti-inflammatory is the usual pair. Stomach burning means I would rather not give Brufen or any other NSAID. We will start colchicine, zero point five milligram twice a day, for three days, with food.
[SEG0061] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0062] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it is still very bad after that, we might add something else, but not an NSAID. Nurse, uric acid, CBC and creatinine today, please.
[SEG0063] person_1 (NURSE): I will draw after you finish. Temperature just now was thirty seven point two, oxygen ninety eight percent, breathing sixteen a minute.
[SEG0064] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thirty seven point two, so not a real fever. Any pus coming, or redness climbing the foot?
[SEG0065] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0066] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No pus. He is not a sugar patient also, last fasting sugar was normal.
[SEG0067] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Any kidney problem?
[SEG0068] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0069] person_2 (DOCTOR): This water tablet, do you swallow it every morning, or do you miss doses?
[SEG0070] person_3 (PATIENT): Sometimes.
[SEG0071] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sometimes you miss? So not every day? Say again.
[SEG0072] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0073] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two or three mornings in a week he forgets. I tell him and he nods only.

[SEG0074] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then the prescription stays twelve point five each morning, but I cannot say he takes all of them. Today, foot up on a pillow, no beer this weekend, ice inside a cloth for ten minutes, not on the skin directly.
[SEG0075] person_3 (PATIENT): Ice.
[SEG0076] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, ice. Does walking make the pain worse?
[SEG0077] person_3 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really.

[SEG0078] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sometimes, not really, I will leave that. Come back if the redness spreads, if fever comes, or if you cannot walk at all. Otherwise I want to see you in one week, with the reports.
[SEG0079] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One week we will come. Should he stop the water tablet?
[SEG0080] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do not stop it on your own. If the tests point to gout we can discuss changing the BP tablet later, not today. Sorry, the cursor jumped. What was the question?
[SEG0081] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Stopping the water tablet, you already said no. His father had kidney stones, if you want that.
[SEG0082] person_2 (DOCTOR): Father, kidney stones, noted. Any operation before?
[SEG0083] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0084] person_1 (NURSE): I am booking serum uric acid, CBC and creatinine downstairs now. You will write the colchicine on the slip, doctor?
[SEG0085] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Colchicine zero point five mg twice daily for three days. Stop it if the loose motions are bad. See me in one week, sooner if it is worsening.
[SEG0086] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay.
